about: THE CHAIN old_gods (Design/content/CHAINS.md; the page is Design/content/chains/old_gods.md): a vow made to the sea in a bad hour, and the price of keeping it and of breaking it. In a gale the steersman says to vow Saint Martin a candle the length of the keel and the hand says to vow the sea a share; the gales cut the dune at Walichrum and a Roman merchant's altar stands out of it, 'for goods kept safe', with three silver pennies of the last century lying among the green coins; a priest of Saint Martin's at Traiectum reads it and wants it gone before midsummer; a Danish skipper at Ripa asks the house to the feast at winter's start in the hall at Hleidr, where a horse is eaten and a lot is lifted; the priest hears of it; and the next summer, on the dune, the stone is buried, raised, signed with the cross or broken. Fourteen cards (eleven harbour, two sea, one crew), four endings (flags ch_old_gods_end_buried, ch_old_gods_end_church, ch_old_gods_end_custom, ch_old_gods_end_broken). History: the buried ending is what happened (the altars lay under the dune until January 1647); changed: changed_walichrum_chapel, changed_nehalennia_remembered, changed_nehalennia_broken. The vow is three flags from the first card (ch_old_gods_vow_martin, ch_old_gods_vow_sea, ch_old_gods_vow_none) and two for its paying (ch_old_gods_paid_martin, ch_old_gods_paid_sea); the hard road in each finale asks that exactly the one who was promised has been paid, that nothing was taken from the stone (ch_old_gods_took) and that the priest was not lied to (ch_old_gods_denied). An unpaid vow brings the card s06 back at sea. Lasting costs: ch_old_gods_watched (a priest who remembers), ch_old_gods_shrine_breaker (the island and the hand remember). Cast (Design/content/spine.json): cast.crew.ravn (the hand) and cast.crew.aldger (the steersman), or a Norse hand and a Frisian steersman of the forge; the bishop is cast.hamacar until 806 and is never named in the words. Everyone else is an ordinary invented person whom the forge names. Nobody in the chain knows the goddess's name but the priest who reads it, and he has met it in no book (lore/gods_cult.md 3.1; dossiers/walichrum.md 8). Waits are flags that lapse (ch_old_gods_owe_wait 150 days, _heard_wait 30, _dune_wait 120, _end_wait 30 to 90). Every chain card after the first has a high weight and a 'when' that asks for the last flag, so it comes on the first call at its port. Every option's 'note' names its outcome text (chain_old_gods.<card>.out_<option>), which the engine does not show yet. Words: Data/writing/chain_old_gods.json. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: at sea in hard weather, any year before 840. The steersman (cast.crew.aldger) and the hand (cast.crew.ravn) each say what a man does. Sources: vows in danger among heathens and Christians alike (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 19, 27, 30: the old man at Birka who says the Christians' god has helped many of them at sea; the Svear who vow a fast and alms to Christ on merchants' advice); the Christian vow of wax, a fast or a pilgrimage in a storm, in the miracle books of every abbey on the coast (lore/gods_cult.md 9 and 10.2; lore/sea_lore.md 11.3); a candle 'of a man's measure' is a miracle-book habit, and the keel's length is ours (?). Saint Martin is Utrecht's patron and his day, 11 November, closes the sea. Sets ch_old_gods_1 and one of ch_old_gods_vow_martin, ch_old_gods_vow_sea, ch_old_gods_vow_none; ch_old_gods_owe_wait runs 150 days.

cards.intention: The wind has backed and the sea comes over the quarter faster than two men can bail. The steersman and the hand each say what a man does now, and they do not say the same thing.

cards.note: Step 2: Walichrum, the first call after step 1, before 846. The gales have cut the dune and one altar stands out. Sources: the altars of Nehalennia at Domburg came out of the dune after a storm in January 1647: a seated woman, a dog, a basket of apples, a ship's prow (dossiers/walichrum.md 2, 6, 7; livius.org 'Nehalennia'; P. Stuart and J. E. Bogaers, Nehalennia, 2001). That a storm uncovered one stone in these years is invented, as lore/sea_lore.md 11.1 allows; that nobody on the island knows her name is the rule of lore/gods_cult.md 3.1. The three silver pennies: three sceattas lay among the Roman coins at the shrine (M. de Man 1899, 'Que sait-on de la plage de Dombourg?'), so somebody about 700 to 750 laid coin there; sceattas are forty years out of use in 793. The idol by the creek and its keeper: Alcuin, Vita Willibrordi c. 14 (about 796), told in our own words. The farm wife is invented (no ordinary name of Walichrum survives). Sets ch_old_gods_2, and ch_old_gods_letters, ch_old_gods_took or ch_old_gods_gave_stone.

cards.note: Step 3 (a side step, drawn under way after step 2: step 4 does not wait for it). The steersman and the hand quarrel about what the stone is. Sources: the Indiculus superstitionum et paganiarum, the list of about 743 in a manuscript of about 800 (no. 7 'what they do upon stones', no. 18 'uncertain places which they honour as holy'), which is the steersman's 'list'; the Lex Frisionum, Additio sapientum XI (about 802, old custom written down): whoever breaks into a shrine and takes any of the holy things is led to the sea, and on the sand the tide covers he is offered to the gods whose temples he violated; it belongs east of the Lauwers and nobody knows that it was carried out in these years, which is what the steersman says (lore/gods_cult.md 1.2, 1.3). The hand's 'receipt' is the votive formula itself. Sets ch_old_gods_3.

cards.note: Step 4: Traiectum, any call after step 2. A priest of Saint Martin's (invented; the forge names him) reads the stone. The words on it are those of a real altar from Domburg (CIL XIII 8793, from memory and from livius.org 'Nehalennia' (?)): Deae Nehalenniae ob merces recte conservatas M. Secund. Silvanus negotiator cretarius Britannicianus v. s. l. m., 'to the goddess Nehalennia, for goods kept safe, Marcus Secundinius Silvanus, dealer in pottery with Britain, paid his vow willingly and deservedly'; the Latin is quoted from the stone and the English is our own. The priest has met her name in no book, which is true of every book he could have had. Willibrord's idol: Alcuin, Vita Willibrordi c. 14. The bishop until 806 is Hamacar (cast.hamacar), not named in the words. The candle: 80 d of wax for a 7.7 m boat is our guess (?). The turn's payout: wax for Saint Martin's at half as much again. Sets ch_old_gods_4, ch_old_gods_paid_martin if the candle is paid; ch_old_gods_heard_wait runs 30 days and ch_old_gods_dune_wait 120.

cards.note: Step 5: Ripa or Sliesthorp, any call after step 2, before 848. A Danish skipper (invented) who knows the hand asks the house to the feast at winter's start in the hall at Hleidr. Sources: the usual offering is a beast killed and eaten together, and horses were eaten at it (Pope Gregory III to Boniface, 732, forbids horseflesh; the bones of meals at Borg, Tisso and Froso; lore/gods_cult.md 4); rites were held in the lord's own hall (Tisso, Lejre; gods_cult.md 6, 7). The ninth-year feast at Lejre is Thietmar of Merseburg I.17, hearsay eighty years on, so the skipper gives it as 'they say' and no number is spoken. An autumn feast: Sigvat's verses of about 1019 have a house holding an offering in autumn; 'winter's start' as the day is ours (?). Wine is the lord's drink (BRIEF.md rule 2). The turn's payout: six casks of Rhenish wine ordered at Ripa at 0.6 over (about 215 d over the price), and a true price word. Sets ch_old_gods_5.

cards.note: Step 6 (the price of a vow not paid; it may come more than once and no other step waits for it): under way, 150 days or more after the vow, while the one who was promised has not been paid. The danger warns first: this card is the warning. Sources: a broken vow is a sin needing penance, and the saint is believed to collect (lore/gods_cult.md 10.2); 'a second card if it is not paid' (gods_cult.md 9, May show); Rimbert c. 19 and 30 for heathens who hold a vow as binding. The swell without wind is ordinary sea: it runs ahead of a gale. A purse over the side pays the sea whoever was promised. Sets ch_old_gods_6; ch_old_gods_paid_sea if the purse goes over; ch_old_gods_owe_wait runs again.

cards.note: Step 7: Hleidr, in the tenth or eleventh month, after step 5, before 849. The feast in the lord's hall, seen from a bench near the bottom, and the bowl of horse. Sources: lore/gods_cult.md 4 (a hall, a killed horse, the meat boiled, ale, a share set aside; the card states what is seen from the edge of the crowd, and the player's man is a stranger there), 6 and 7 (the lord gives the feast in his own hall; there is no priesthood); horseflesh as the mark of a heathen (Gregory III to Boniface, 732; Iceland's exemption in 1000); a Christian who will not eat what was offered, and the trouble it makes (1 Corinthians 8 and 10; popes' letters to missionaries). Lejre's great halls of these centuries are dug (Christensen, Lejre). The steward and the lord are invented and unnamed. Nothing is said of what words were spoken over the beast: bones do not say (gods_cult.md 1.15). Sets ch_old_gods_7, and ch_old_gods_ate if the bowl is not passed on.

cards.note: Step 8: Hleidr, the morning after step 7 (the option's 'then'), or any later call. An old man of the district lifts a lot for a question that can be answered yes or no, and the share vowed to the sea can be given to the water. Sources: the lot is the best-attested act of the old custom: cast in the open by men of standing, answering yes or no to a question put (Rimbert c. 18, 19, 26, 27, 30); the lots are marked slips of wood (the Lex Frisionum's 'teni', twigs; lore/gods_cult.md 5: three slips, a cloth, an old man of the place who lifts one, the answer a word and never a prophecy). Things given to water: weapons and tools in the lake at Tisso (gods_cult.md 4). That a lord asks the lot before sailing: Rimbert c. 19 and 30. The old man is invented; the role is 'lawman' for want of a nearer one (the Funen stones' 'thulr', a speaker). The lot here is an even chance and says only yes or no. Sets ch_old_gods_8, ch_old_gods_paid_sea if the share is given; ch_old_gods_dune_wait runs 120 days.

cards.note: Step 9 (a side step: the finales do not wait for it): Traiectum, thirty days or more after step 4, if the house ate the horse, gave silver to the sea, laid a penny at the stone or took silver from it. The priest who will hear of it. Sources: penance by the book, a term of fasting on bread, water and salt for each sin, and its turning into alms, psalms or silver, which churchmen complained of and took (lore/gods_cult.md 10.3: Theodore's and Egbert's penitentials in England, Halitgar's about 830; eating what was offered to idols, a term; consulting a diviner, a year or more (?)); horseflesh (Gregory III to Boniface, 732); Dorestad's 'multitude of poor' (Rimbert c. 20). Forty days and forty-eight pennies are our tariff (?). The order is the older one: penance first. Sets ch_old_gods_9; ch_old_gods_denied if he is lied to; ch_old_gods_watched if the lie is seen.

cards.note: Step 10, the hub: Walichrum, from the fourth to the ninth month, 120 days or more after step 4 or step 8, before 849. The stone stands clear, and it is buried, raised, signed with the cross or broken. Four options, because the story has four roads; the first asks nothing and is what happened. Sources: the stone went back under the dune and lay there until January 1647 (dossiers/walichrum.md 2, 7); Willibrord broke the idol of Walichrum (Alcuin, Vita Willibrordi c. 14); Pope Gregory's letter of 601 to Mellitus, in Bede (Historia ecclesiastica I.30): do not pull the shrines down, cleanse them and set altars in them, so that the people come to the places they know; Liudger breaking the Frisian shrines and bringing back the treasure in them, of which the king took two thirds (Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.16 (?)); the stone at Westkapelle that Thiofrid of Echternach (about 1103) says bears Willibrord's blood, perhaps a Roman altar (dossiers/walichrum.md 7); no church is recorded at Walichrum in these years (walichrum.md 2), so the chapel is history changed. An English skipper leaving apples is invented. The clerk and the farm wife are invented. Sets ch_old_gods_10 and one of ch_old_gods_road_buried, _road_custom, _road_church, _road_broken; ch_old_gods_end_wait runs 30 to 90 days.

cards.note: Finale, the ending 'buried' (what happened): Walichrum, sixty days or more after step 10. The dune is whole; the islanders are left alone by the bishop's men and by the Danes, and pay in what they have. Sources: Walichrum's wool, hides and cloth from marsh sheep, and the abbeys' Frisian cloth round the Scheldt mouth (dossiers/walichrum.md 4); the Banjaard shoals off the island's north-west corner and the creek behind the dunes (walichrum.md 1); Thiofrid on the islanders, stubborn and taught only by miracles (walichrum.md 7). The altars lie under the sand until January 1647. Pays 14 bolts of Frisian cloth (about 670 d) and the grand reward unlock_pilot_scheldt (the Scheldt mouth and the Banjaard); the hard road adds unlock_factor_walichrum (a house on the island that keeps the house's wool and a true tally). Sets ch_old_gods_end_buried and ch_old_gods_done.

cards.note: Finale, the ending 'church' (history changed: changed_walichrum_chapel): Traiectum, sixty days or more after step 10. A chapel of turf and oak stands on the dune with the signed stone as its altar's foot, a lifetime and more before any church is recorded on that coast (the churches of Saint Willibrord at Westkapelle and Oostkapelle are of the early eleventh century; churchyard burial on this coast begins in the tenth: dossiers/walichrum.md 5, 6). The bishop (cast.hamacar until 806; Ricfried and Frederick after; unnamed in the words) speaks. Sources: Gregory to Mellitus, 601, in Bede I.30, in our own words; the tale that Willibrord bled on a stone on Walcheren (Thiofrid, about 1103), here beginning three hundred years early; Saint Martin's privileges and its tenth of the king's dues (Data/story/unlocks_793.json unlock_charter_traiectum). Pays 8 casks of Rhenish wine and 240 d (about 720 d) and the grand reward unlock_charter_traiectum; the hard road adds unlock_relic_willibrord_stone (a chip of the signed stone in a linen bag: a contact relic of the place, which an honest bishop can give). Sets ch_old_gods_end_church and ch_old_gods_done.

cards.note: Finale, the ending 'custom' (history changed: changed_nehalennia_remembered): Walichrum, ninety days or more after step 10. The stone stands on turf facing the sea and seamen of three peoples lay things at it without a name to say; a Danish skipper (invented) brings the thanks of the lord at Hleidr. Sources: baptised people offering at stones and 'uncertain places' (Indiculus 7, 9, 18); the offer act: bread, ale, a coin, a bit of the cargo (lore/gods_cult.md 6); gods chosen for results (Rimbert c. 27); felag, 'to lay property together', on the rune stones of Hedeby and Aarhus, and a lord's ring kept whole (Data/story/unlocks_793.json unlock_partner_felagi, unlock_heirloom_arm_ring); silver by weight among the Danes before their own coin. Pays 400 d of hack-silver and three timbers of marten (about 760 d) and the grand reward unlock_partner_felagi, or unlock_heirloom_arm_ring for the man who keeps his own keel; the hard road gives both. The cost that lasts: ch_old_gods_watched (the priest at Traiectum knows the name of the man who raised her). Sets ch_old_gods_end_custom and ch_old_gods_done.

cards.note: Finale, the ending 'broken' (history changed: changed_nehalennia_broken): Traiectum, thirty days or more after step 10. Under the stone lay a pit of coin; it is weighed before the count's man, two parts to the king and one to Saint Martin. Sources: Liudger sent to destroy the shrines of the Frisians, and the treasure found in them, of which the king took two thirds (Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.16 (?)); Roman coins at the shrine by the hundred, with three sceattas among them (M. de Man 1899); gold among them is our guess (?). The islanders did not burn their houses over it, they stopped selling: Thiofrid's islanders are stubborn. A lord's protection: Data/story/unlocks_793.json unlock_title_lords_protection. The count's man is invented. Pays 640 d (two pounds and eight ounces by tale) and the grand reward unlock_title_lords_protection; the man who gives his share to the poor of the church takes no silver and is given unlock_charter_traiectum beside it; the man who sends half back to the island takes 320 d and is forgiven there. The cost that lasts: ch_old_gods_shrine_breaker (the island sells him nothing; the hand rows and no more), unless half goes back (ch_old_gods_island_mended). In later years: no altars come out of the dune in January 1647, and nobody ever reads her name. Sets ch_old_gods_end_broken and ch_old_gods_done.
